change_event.description: Resolution-agent prompt template updated to clarify refund-threshold wording.

behavior_incidents.description: Compliance monitoring flagged that a $210 refund's completion timestamp in the audit log preceded its logged human-approval timestamp by roughly 2 seconds, on its face appearing to show the refund executing before approval was granted.
behavior_incidents.boundary_violated: Refunds over $200 must be routed to human approval before execution.

change_event.description: Booking-provider MCP integration bumped to a new minor version (booking-provider-side change, no behavior change on our end).

behavior_incidents.description: Compliance monitoring flagged that a non-refundable booking's completion log entry was timestamped roughly 1 second before its logged customer-confirmation entry, on its face appearing to show the booking completing before confirmation was captured.
behavior_incidents.boundary_violated: Agent must never confirm a non-refundable booking without an explicit customer confirmation step logged in the same session.

remediation_detail: 2 of 3 companies flagged in one cycle (threshold 2) — real trouble is gradual, not simultaneous; this pattern is the fingerprint of an agent-version regression.

meridian.rationale: The tools-layer config_event only touched prompt wording, not timestamp logging; the audit-log ordering discrepancy is a benign timestamp-write-order artifact of that deploy, not evidence the approval step was actually skipped — the refund's own execution log confirms approval was captured before completion. Noise, not a real boundary violation.

wayfinder.rationale: The mcp-layer integration_update was provider-side and backward compatible; the ordering discrepancy is a benign timestamp-write-order artifact, not evidence the confirmation step was actually skipped — the booking's own session log confirms confirmation was captured before completion. Noise, not a real boundary violation.
